title: Why bebop did not become his style: Armstrong and Joe Louis in their prime
summary: Having heard Armstrong in his prime, Butler says bebop came too late for him, comparing it to Joe Louis; he chose to refine what made him king rather than sound like others.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, now, did you -- since you were studying all this advanced harmony and stuff, then bebop must have made pretty clear sense to you then, huh?
Yeah, yes, yes, yes, --
You didn't have any problem with it then?

Oh, no problems, but you see bebop, you see, what comes of your experience and, and, and, and, to you, you see, were I born in 1927, bebop would have been beautiful to me, but, see, I had heard Louis Armstrong in his prime.
Uh-huh.
So, bebop was beautiful, but I heard Louis Armstrong in his prime, you understand?
For example, a young man who said, Cassius Clay is something else, but I've seen Joe Louis in his prime. You see, understand?
Uh-huh.

I know. I've seen Joe Louis in his prime, you see, and Joe Louis -- when he creeped up on a man at that point, that was it. He don't run nowhere. There is no running when Joe Louis tag a man and he's finished them off. That's all.
See what I mean?
Uh-huh.
This is what I've seen, so I can compare.

So, what I said was this, as I said, if you the king, what made you king? What were you playing when you was king? Do what you was doing, only do it greater. Refine it. So, therefore, I said, why should I go into this when my faculties are not poised for that?
So, what I would do, I would do what I'd been doing but refine it, or make it more -- crystallize it more.
Uh-huh.
Refine it. But if I started to do that, I would be sounding like them.
Uh-huh.
And then, if you sound like somebody, well, -- you say, he reminds me of so and so.
Uh-huh.
And time has passed too long for me to
be reminding of anybody else.
Uh-huh.
